verdict.label: Worth checking
verdict.headline: Rey Cortiço Lunch
verdict.reason: Rey Cortiço is worth a quick check for lunch, but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should let the sandbars work without overdoing it.

conversationalSummary.text: Rey Cortiço at lunch is the best available option, but the wind angle isn’t great and it could easily feel more awkward than worth it. Before you leave, check the Surfline cams and the MEO Beachcam for that spot—if it doesn’t look much cleaner than expected, I’d pass. With a mid dropping tide you might get some punchy sets, but confidence is low, so the cam check should really decide it.

best.explanation: Rey Cortiço looks like a fun-sized north coast window for Rare window, Low confidence: 0.6-0.9 m, 58 kJ, 8 s period, consistent 67/100, and wind is the main risk.  An open beach break where the sandbanks decide everything; this is best for quiet, punchy peaks when Lagide is too small; 6-9s at mid tide can turn Belgas punchy and rippable, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot.

ranked.explanation: Meio da Baia looks like a fun-sized window for Worth checking, Medium confidence: 0.6-0.9 m, 76 kJ, 8 s period, consistent 72/100, and wind is the main risk.  An inconsistent Baía spot that can work well when north-northwest swell reaches the bay; this is best for bodyboard sessions when the bay is clean, there is enough period and size, and the forecast shows a defined wave; 6-9s at mid tide can make exposed beaches like Belgas / Almagreira / Cerro / Meio da Baia sharp and rippable.  Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot; Meio da Baia may feel too soft without more push.
